entities.text: HIGH COURT OF GUJARAT AT AHMEDABAD
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: ORAL ORDER 1. RULE returnable forthwith.
Mr. Dhawan Jayswal, learned Additional Public Prosecutor, waives service of notice of rule on behalf of the respondent - State.

2. The present application is filed under Section 439 of the Code of Criminal Procedure, 1973, for regular bail in connection with FIR being 11209017220955 of 2022 registered with Himatnagar (Rural) Police Station, Sabarkantha for offence under Sections 363, 366 and 376 (2)(j)(n) of the Indian Penal Code and Under Sections 4, 5(l), 6, 11(4), 12 and 17 of the Protection of Children from Sexual Offences Act.
3.

entities.text: Protection of Children from Sexual Offences Act
entities.label: STATUTE

sentences.text: Learned Advocate appearing on behalf of the applicant submits that considering the nature of the offence, the applicant may be enlarged on regular bail by imposing suitable conditions.

4. Learned APP appearing on behalf of the respondent - R/CR.MA/3839/2023 ORDER DATED: 20/02/2023 State has opposed grant of regular bail looking to the nature and gravity of the offence.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Learned Advocates appearing on behalf of the respective parties do not press for further reasoned order.

6. Having heard the learned advocates for the parties and perusing the material placed on record and taking into consideration the facts of the case, nature of allegations, gravity of offences, role attributed to the accused, without discussing the evidence in detail, this Court is of the opinion that this is a fit case to exercise the discretion and enlarge the applicant on regular bail.

entities.text: Protection of Children from Sexual Offences Act
entities.label: STATUTE

sentences.text: (c) Considering the history given before the Doctor by the victim herself, it reflects that she knows the applicant since last about 2 years and is having affair with him and wants to marry him.
It is further revealed in the history that since last about 2 years, time and again she had physical relationship with him with her full consent.

It is further revealed that since 16.11.2022, out of her volition, she accompanied the applicant and stayed together at different places and during the period also she had physical relations with the applicant with her full consent.
R/CR.MA/3839/2023 ORDER DATED: 20/02/2023 (d) they stayed together for approximately 56 days.
The applicant is aged about 21 years and having relation with the victim.
Considering the history given by him before the Doctor, he confirms the facts volunteered before the Doctor as history.

(e) In view of the fact that both were having physical relationship out of their relations and of her own volition, though considering the age prescribed under the Act does not recognize consent where the victim is less than 18 years, considering the age and maturity of the victim, I deem it fit to release the applicant on bail, pending trial as charge-sheet is already filed.

8. This Court has also taken into consideration the law laid down by the Hon'ble Apex Court in the case of Sanjay Chandra Vs. Central Bureau of Investigation, reported in [2012] 1 SCC 40.
9.

entities.text: Sanjay Chandra Vs. Central Bureau of Investigation, reported in [2012] 1 SCC 40
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Hence, the present application is allowed.

entities.text: Jigarsinh Rajusinh Parmar vs State Of Gujarat
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: The authorities will release the applicant only if he is not required in connection with any other offence for the time being.
If breach of any of the above conditions is committed, the Sessions Judge concerned will be free to issue warrant or take appropriate action in the matter.
Bail bond to be executed before the lower Court having jurisdiction to try the case.
It will be open for the concerned Court to delete, modify and/or relax any of the above conditions, in accordance with law.
At the trial, the trial Court shall not be influenced by the prima facie observations made by this Court in the present order.
12. Rule is made absolute to the aforesaid extent.
Direct service is permitted.
